skill.name: stop-slop
skill.description: Use when drafting, editing, or reviewing prose so the agent removes predictable AI writing tells and returns direct, specific, human-sounding copy.
whenToUse: Cleaning up marketing copy, launch posts, landing-page sections, newsletters, or social drafts that sound AI-written
Reviewing executive updates, internal docs, or productivity writing for filler, passive voice, and formulaic structure
Turning generic AI prose into direct prose with concrete actors, specifics, and varied sentence rhythm
Scoring a draft before publishing using directness, rhythm, trust, authenticity, and density

keyConcepts.explanation: Cut throat-clearing openers, emphasis crutches, business jargon, adverbs, self-referential asides, and vague importance claims. The skill points to a reference list of common offenders.
Avoid AI-shaped patterns such as binary contrasts, negative listings, dramatic fragments, rhetorical setups, false transformation arcs, and three-item rhythm.
Every sentence should name a human actor when possible. Passive constructions and inanimate abstractions doing human verbs hide responsibility and flatten the prose.
Replace sweeping claims, lazy extremes, and sentences like 'the implications are significant' with the exact person, action, constraint, number, or consequence.
Write to the reader directly instead of narrating from above. 'You' and concrete scenes beat distant generalizations about people, teams, or markets.
Before delivery, rate directness, rhythm, trust, authenticity, and density from 1 to 10. Below 35 out of 50 means revise before handing over the draft.

apiReference.purpose: Use the upstream skill by copying its SKILL.md into the agent's skill directory.
apiReference.example:
git clone https://github.com/hardikpandya/stop-slop
mkdir -p ~/.codex/skills/stop-slop
cp stop-slop/SKILL.md ~/.codex/skills/stop-slop/SKILL.md

apiReference.purpose: A reusable prompt shape for applying the skill to any draft.
apiReference.example:
Apply stop-slop to this draft. Remove filler phrases, binary contrasts, passive voice, vague declaratives, em dashes, and pull-quote endings. Keep the meaning. Return the revised draft, then score directness, rhythm, trust, authenticity, and density out of 10.

DRAFT:
<paste text>

apiReference.purpose: Run a compact checklist after writing or editing prose.
apiReference.example: Check this draft for adverbs, passive voice, inanimate subjects doing human actions, Wh- sentence starters, 'here is what' openers, 'not X but Y' contrasts, repeated sentence length, punchy one-liner paragraph endings, em dashes, vague significance claims, distant narrator voice, and meta-joiners.

gotchas: Do not preserve AI-sounding phrasing just because it is grammatically correct; the point is to remove recognizable patterns.
Do not remove specificity while compressing. A shorter generic sentence is still slop.
The skill forbids em dashes, but one upstream example still contains one; follow the rule, not that example.
Active voice does not mean aggressive voice. Name the actor and action without manufacturing hype.
A pull-quote ending can sound polished and still feel fake. Rewrite it as a normal sentence or cut it.
Use the scoring rubric as a revision gate, not as decoration after the draft is already done.
